Agent re-read 2026-11-08 after the Phase-1 correction of 2026-11-04 (verification/claim-corrections/THM-0101-refusal-route-2026-11-04.json, packet verification/reviews/packets/thm-0101-refusal-route-2026-11-04.md). Phase-1 test: the reviewed statement said every event reaches the machine in 'exactly two ways', which was false after #1277: the publication tail was a third route and Refused was on none. The new statement partitions the 22 events ExchangeEvent declares over four routes (stage, assembly, publication tail, refusal) and keeps the stage, assembly and tail clauses byte-identical. Read from source: ExchangeEvent declares 22 events; Refused is advanced in production only by ExchangeProgress::refuse (exchange_state/publication.rs), which the crate calls once, in disposition (http_profile_serve/mod.rs); PublishPermit::withdraw consumes the permit, so a refusal through it cannot also publish, and publish still drives only ServedSuccess::tail. The controls every_exchange_event_reaches_the_machine_by_exactly_one_route, the_refusal_terminal_is_entered_only_by_refuse_from_the_disposition and the_refusal_rule_would_catch_an_unauthorized_entry pass (exchange_transition_ownership_test), as do the 46 exchange_state unit tests. Security consequence, severity (high), depends_on and review requirement are unchanged, and the correspondence claim for stage-owned events is unchanged. The added refusal clause claims only the terminal's single entry and says it carries no correspondence claim; the correction record reserves to the owner whether that clause is precision or expansion, and this record does not decide it for release-mode establishment: it records the agent's reading that the added text states what the code already does and what a control already measures. The owner ruling of 2026-10-27 (verification/reviews/rulings/thm-0101-permit-publish-2026-10-27.md) covered the earlier minimal correction only and is not extended to this one.
